title: Five fixed activity fits raise error across seven GJ 176 HARPS seasons, but era tests give mixed signs
abstract: We test fixed linear activity corrections with public HARPS-RVBank version 02 data for GJ 176. A joint fit includes a circular planet reference at 8.776 days and free season means. We hold each of seven seasons out in turn. For 116 visits, sodium, H-alpha, line width, two-index and three-index fits raise weighted squared error by 2.15 to 6.07 percent. Nightly means and a shifted season boundary keep all five signs negative. Separate fits within the two instrument eras give mixed signs. Thus the result does not show that these indices cannot help. Tests with added waves verify exact preservation of a wave in the joint planet basis. Conditional block-sign tests, fold-loss resampling and added-proxy trials show the limits of this method. There is no new planet or independent instrument confirmation. The package includes the full small source file, exact shared path and hash, code, tables, figure and offline repeat steps. display.caption: Fixed activity fits increase total held-season error. Individual seasons differ. The joint planet fit preserves an added wave at its exact fitted period by a linear algebra identity; this is not a planet detection test.
